key_insight: A structured LLM workflow (HeLIX) extracted complex hepatology EHR data with physician-level accuracy, nearly matching manual chart review.
clinical_relevance: If validated in real-world settings, this could speed up cohort building, retrospective studies, and registry creation while reducing chart-review burden.
method: Prospective validation on 50 simulated high-complexity hepatology discharge summaries
LLM used zero-shot structured chain-of-thought prompting with three layers: reasoning trace, schema enforcement, and evidence verification
Compared model output against consensus manual chart review across 45 clinical variables
evidence_signal: Across 2,250 data points, the model achieved 99.24% extraction accuracy, F1 0.98 for binary diagnostic variables, and 2/2250 hallucinations.
watch_item: Results came from simulated discharge summaries, so performance may differ on real-world EHR notes with broader variability and workflow integration challenges.
paper_title: General-purpose large language models can achieve physician-level accuracy in complex medical data extraction
